definition: Entitle means to give someone the right to have or do something.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word entitle. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know entitle should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Twenty years of service entitle every ranger to a lifetime pass through any gate in the park system.
Allow stops short of entitle — what is allowed today can be forbidden tomorrow; a right must be honored.
Guarantee goes further than entitle — an entitled customer may claim the refund; a guaranteed one receives it without asking.

A license is official permission from an authority, recorded on paper — a credential that certifies you may drive, fish, or practice medicine. Entitle is broader and needs no certificate: a ticket stub, a warranty, or a will can entitle you, creating a claim that must be honored.

To permit is simply to allow — a favor or leave that can be taken back whenever the giver pleases. Entitle creates a standing right instead: once a rule or a purchase serves to entitle you to something, it is owed to you until the rule itself changes.

By the end, even the shareholder newsletters described the aging chairman as titular, and nobody at headquarters objected.
Entitle means to give someone the right to have or do something.
Her grandfather's will entitles each grandchild to one item from the workshop before the auction — Ada chose the dented level that had built three barns.
Entitle creates a claim you can stand on: if a warranty entitles you to repairs, the shop is not doing you a favor — it owes you.
Permission can be revoked and kindness can run out, but an entitlement must be honored until the rule that granted it changes.
Entitle is the general-purpose right-granter: tickets, warranties, bylaws, wills.
Reach for its unit-mate enfranchise only when the right in question is the vote.
And note the modern edge on entitled — 'he acted entitled' means he claimed rights nobody granted; the verb itself stays neutral.
